name: gap_continuation_momentum_5s_2
author: adapted from claude_strategist
thesis: Large gaps (> 1.5%) in Nifty50 stocks tend to continue in the gap direction for the first 30-60 minutes because they are typically news-driven (results, upgrades, block deals). Unlike small gaps that fill, large gaps represent genuine re-pricing. The first 15-minute range AFTER the gap gives a tradeable range: breakout in the gap direction is a continuation signal. Edge persists because retail traders often fade large gaps, creating opposing flow that the trend absorbs.
mechanism: Large opening gaps that hold above the prior range indicate a genuine overnight revaluation. Participants who missed the gap chase the move, while short-sellers who are wrong-footed cover into the trend. The resulting buy pressure sustains the gap direction for the first 30-60 minutes until the new equilibrium is established.

exit.signal_exit: close crosses back inside post-gap ORB range

weaknesses: Slippage is highest at open (5+ bps); large gaps attract aggressive order flow
Very low frequency — gaps > 1.5% in liquid Nifty50 names happen a few times per month
Gap can be driven by one-off event (delisting, fraud) where continuation logic doesn't apply
prior_art: Gap continuation — opposite of gap fill. Well-documented threshold: gaps > 1-1.5% tend to continue.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
